description.narrative: (Uganda): USAID strives to increase household and community access to improved sanitation and water services; promote the adoption and expansion of key hygiene behaviors in homes, schools, and health facilities (in partnership with Rotary International); and strengthen district water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) governance for sustainable services.With FY 2022 funds, the Uganda Sanitation for Health Activity (USHA) will implement activities in 21 districts, with priority in northern districts. Activities will include expanding access to improved sanitation through the market-based sanitation implementation approach, community-led total sanitation and verification of open defecation free communities, and expanding community water access through implementing a pro-poor strategy. USHA will consolidate its social and behavior change campaign and strengthen fecal sludge management business models by establishing better market connections. USHA will provide technical assistance for the district-led national rollout of market-based sanitation and continue to consolidate capacity-building for districts in aspects of planning, information and data management, advocacy, and coordination. School WASH interventions will focus on completing infrastructure improvements and promoting WASH-friendly performance. At a national level, USHA will support the Government of Uganda (GOU) to implement the National Sanitation Marketing Guidelines to facilitate increased private sector participation in achieving universal basic sanitation in priority populations. USHA will also document and disseminate key learnings to national level stakeholders to inform the scale-up of appropriate and workable implementation approaches.USHA's interventions will support the GOU's COVID-19 response through facilitating improved water access, uptake of key behavior practices like handwashing, and infection prevention and control in households, communities, and institutions..
